title: TEMPO (Tracking, Engagement, Messaging & Participant Outreach): automated survey scheduling and participant messaging for longitudinal studies
description:
A self-hosted server for research studies that send scheduled surveys and reminders. TEMPO sits between a study's survey database of record and its messaging providers, turning a declarative timeline of study messages into precisely timed, auditable outreach. Any protocol whose contacts are driven by participant dates — longitudinal cohorts, momentary-assessment sampling, recurring survey cycles, retention and compensation sequences, trial follow-up schedules — can be expressed as a timeline spec and run without manual sending.

Capabilities include momentary-assessment (EMA) prompt delivery on fixed grids with exact-second firing and protocol-compliant skip handling; recurring survey cycles with conditional follow-up cadences that stop on response; visit, at-home and compensation reminders; just-in-time personal survey-link resolution; a password-gated coordinator dashboard for completion tracking and outgoing-message review; and a daily send-reconciliation audit. Delivery is defended by opt-out enforcement, quiet hours, append-only idempotency ledgers, provider-history arbitration against double-sends, send claims, a runtime kill switch, and bounded catch-up windows.

Extracted from servers running NIH-funded longitudinal research. The repository contains source files only: no participant data or credentials appear in the working tree or its history, and the message timeline ships as a synthetic example rather than a real protocol.
